## Before submitting

- [ ] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [x] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

C++ frontend API or graph construction; Python API or bindings

## Summary

Follow-up to #1548. It handles the P2 that the Codex review raised there ([discussion](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1548#discussion_r4236344804)).

1. In layernorm training, a `MEAN` or `INV_VARIANCE` whose dims the caller did not set now takes the dims set on the other stat. Before, it took the dims inferred from `scale`, or `{N,1,...}` without a scale.
2. `MEAN` and `INV_VARIANCE` with different dims return `INVALID_VALUE` ("Layernorm MEAN and INV_VARIANCE dims differ.") from `validate()`.
3. The no-scale ambiguity check (#1548) now also accepts `MEAN` dims, not only `INV_VARIANCE` dims. Its message reads "set the MEAN or INV_VARIANCE dims".
4. The Python graph's layernorm shape inference (`_pygraph._NORM_FWD_INFER`) applies the same rule, so the dims reported after `validate()` match the C++ node.
   - The structured builder fills both stats' dims when `graph.layernorm()` runs, before the caller can set either. So the layernorm spec now names `mean` and `inv_var` as `reinfer` ports.
   - `validate()` re-infers a `reinfer` port unless the caller assigned its dims, and a stat follows its sibling only when that sibling's dims were user-assigned.
   - Without this, a stat the caller did not set kept `[2,1,1]` after `validate()` while C++ had `[2,8,1]`, so a buffer allocated from it was 8x short. This was caught in review.
   - A re-inferred port keeps a stride the caller set. Without that, padded stats such as `[16,2,1]` would build and run with a row-major layout instead of being refused. Also caught in review.

## Why

Example: scale-free training, `X = {2,8,64}`, with only `INV_VARIANCE = {2,8,1}` set.
- Before this change, `validate()` inferred `MEAN = {2,1,1}` and accepted the graph.
- `build_operation_graph()` then failed with `CUDNN_STATUS_BAD_PARAM_SHAPE_MISMATCH`. This was measured in the #1548 review on cuDNN 9.27.

Explicitly mismatched stats failed the same way. With this change both are settled at `validate()`: the first case is served and the second is refused.

## API and compatibility impact

- Graphs with a scale, and graphs whose stats dims are both unset or both set and equal, behave as before.
- A graph with one stat's dims set used to fail at `build_operation_graph()` whenever the other stat's inferred dims differed. It now gets matching dims.
- adalayernorm and rmsnorm are unchanged. rmsnorm has no `MEAN`.

## Testing

All on cuDNN 9.27, with the extension rebuilt from this branch:

| Where | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| C++ tests | `tests "[validate]"` (the layernorm case adds a one-stat-set case for each stat, plus a mismatch case with and without a scale) | 9 test cases / 95 assertions passed |
| C++ samples | `samples "[layernorm],[adalayernorm],[rmsnorm]"` | B200 21/21; H100, A100 17 passed / 4 skipped |
| Python | `pytest -m "L0 or L1 or L2 or L3 or L4" norm/graph/test_layernorm.py norm/graph/test_rmsnorm.py` | B200 58 passed; H100, A100 54 passed / 4 skipped |
| Python, B200 | `pytest -n 6 -m "L0 or L1 or L2 or L3 or L4" norm/graph` | 5193 passed, 1 skipped |
| Python, previous head 4cb5b8110 | the new one-stat test, which checks dims right after `validate()` | both cells fail (`[2, 8, 1] == [2, 1, 1]`), as expected |

New Python tests:
- `test_layernorm_without_scale_one_stat_dims_state_the_axes[mean, inv_var]` executes and checks Y and both stats against a reference.
- `test_layernorm_refuses_stats_with_different_dims[no_scale, scale]`.
- `test_layernorm_stats_keep_a_stride_the_caller_set`. It fails on 249094db9 with `[8, 1, 1] == [16, 2, 1]`.

Part of #188.

[P1] Refresh inferred statistics before returning from validate()

The structured builder eagerly fills both statistics, so this helper runs before the caller can set either returned tensor's dimensions. Later `validate()` skips inference for nonempty Python dimensions and does not synchronize the dimensions inferred by C++. For a scale-free training input `[2,8,64]`, setting only `mean` to `[2,8,1]` leaves Python `inv_var.get_dim()` at `[2,1,1]` after successful validation, while its native tensor is already `[2,8,1]`; setting only `inv_var` produces the symmetric problem. Recompute non-explicit statistics dimensions from the explicitly set counterpart, or synchronize validated native properties before `validate()` returns, and assert both Python shapes immediately after validation in the regression tests. This is approval-blocking because the metadata mismatch can lead to invalid memory writes.

The earlier [high-risk buffer-size finding](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1552#discussion_r4236706137) is resolved. Both statistics now have the correct Python and native dimensions immediately after `validate()`, whichever statistic the caller specifies.

Validation: all 57 committed LayerNorm/RMSNorm tests passed on SM100 with cuDNN 9.27, plus four focused regression controls. Buffers allocated immediately after validation passed both `execute` and `execute_plan_at_index`, an independent FP64 reference, and three changed-input CUDA Graph replays per inference direction. The native extension is unchanged from the previously tested revision. All five PR files integrate cleanly with current develop. CI pipeline 72862813 is still running; no duplicate run requested.

One nonblocking P2 below: re-inference overwrites explicit strides and bypasses rejection of an already-unsupported padded statistics layout. No remaining approval-blocking finding.

<!-- codex-fe-review:github-only:vedaanta:1552:249094db991f20125f4525181aa0db8520f11ce5:complete -->

[P2] Preserve explicitly assigned statistics strides during re-inference

The new branch also executes the unconditional `out_t.stride = _row_major_stride(...)`, even when `stride_assigned` is true. For `X=[2,8,64]`, `scale=[1,1,64]`, and both statistics configured with `set_stride([16,2,1])` without `set_dim`, `validate()` now replaces those strides with `[8,1,1]`. Please preserve user-assigned strides independently of whether dimensions were inferred. This is nonblocking because the demonstrated padded layout was already unsupported; the regression is silently changing its meaning instead of retaining the backend rejection.

Fixed in 4a270ae3a.
- A re-inferred port keeps a user-assigned stride. A port whose dims were empty still gets the row-major stride as before, so behaviour outside the `reinfer` path is unchanged.
- New test `test_layernorm_stats_keep_a_stride_the_caller_set`: X=[2,8,64], scale=[1,1,64], both stats `set_stride([16,2,1])` and no dims set. It checks the strides right after `validate()`.
  - On 249094db9 it fails with `[8, 1, 1] == [16, 2, 1]`; here it passes.
- `test_layernorm.py` + `test_rmsnorm.py`: B200 58 passed; H100 and A100 54 passed / 4 skipped.

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `4a270ae3a39b68de00033e639a42a509202235a9` against `34e8eaa87d832626cdc1691bec2558dc33e60c51`. The [explicit-stride P2](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1552#discussion_r4237008178) is resolved: caller-assigned strides survive Python and native validation, and the backend again rejects unsupported padded statistics before execution. The guard preserves the previous behavior outside re-inferred outputs.

All 17 focused checks passed on SM100 with cuDNN 9.27, including the new regression test, both explicit-stride rejection controls, and the original dimension/allocation controls with both execution entrypoints and changed-input CUDA Graph replay. The two-file follow-up leaves native code unchanged and integrates cleanly with current develop. Reused the preceding revision’s broader 57-test normalization coverage; the owner’s CI run 72874620 is underway.

No new actionable findings. My existing approval remains in place.

inline_comments.body:
[P1] Refresh inferred statistics before returning from validate()

The structured builder eagerly fills both statistics, so this helper runs before the caller can set either returned tensor's dimensions. Later `validate()` skips inference for nonempty Python dimensions and does not synchronize the dimensions inferred by C++. For a scale-free training input `[2,8,64]`, setting only `mean` to `[2,8,1]` leaves Python `inv_var.get_dim()` at `[2,1,1]` after successful validation, while its native tensor is already `[2,8,1]`; setting only `inv_var` produces the symmetric problem. A caller allocating outputs from those validated dimensions gets 2 FP32 elements instead of 16. `build_operation_graph()` subsequently changes the metadata, but both public execute paths still forward the original undersized tensor's pointer to the native launcher (confirmed by interception before launch), exposing an out-of-bounds output write on this newly accepted configuration. Recompute non-explicit statistics dimensions from the explicitly set counterpart, or synchronize validated native properties before `validate()` returns, and assert both Python shapes immediately after validation in the regression tests. This is approval-blocking because the metadata mismatch can lead to invalid memory writes.

Fixed in 93910ee95.
- The layernorm spec now marks `mean` / `inv_var` as `reinfer` ports. `validate()` re-infers them unless the caller assigned them, and a stat follows its sibling only when that sibling is user-assigned.
- The test asserts both Python dims right after `validate()`. It fails on 4cb5b8110 for both stats (`[2, 8, 1] == [2, 1, 1]`) and passes here.
- Results:
  - `test_layernorm.py` + `test_rmsnorm.py`: B200 57 passed; H100 and A100 53 passed / 4 skipped.
  - Full `norm/graph` on B200: 5193 passed, 1 skipped.
- Merged develop (249094db9) to pick up the #1551 tier fix.

[P2] Preserve explicitly assigned statistics strides during re-inference

The new branch also executes the unconditional `out_t.stride = _row_major_stride(...)`, even when `stride_assigned` is true. For `X=[2,8,64]`, `scale=[1,1,64]`, and both statistics configured with `set_stride([16,2,1])` without `set_dim`, `validate()` now replaces those strides with `[8,1,1]`. On both SM100 and H100, the previous head preserves the layout and rejects these padded statistics during operation-graph construction; this head instead builds and executes, producing incorrect/NaN values in 15/16 logical elements when the caller supplies the declared padded views. Please preserve user-assigned strides independently of whether dimensions were inferred. This is nonblocking because the demonstrated padded layout was already unsupported; the regression is silently changing its meaning instead of retaining the backend rejection.

Fixed in 4a270ae3a.
- A re-inferred port keeps a user-assigned stride. A port whose dims were empty still gets the row-major stride as before, so behaviour outside the `reinfer` path is unchanged.
- New test `test_layernorm_stats_keep_a_stride_the_caller_set`: X=[2,8,64], scale=[1,1,64], both stats `set_stride([16,2,1])` and no dims set. It checks the strides right after `validate()`.
  - On 249094db9 it fails with `[8, 1, 1] == [16, 2, 1]`; here it passes.
- `test_layernorm.py` + `test_rmsnorm.py`: B200 58 passed; H100 and A100 54 passed / 4 skipped.
